front: Je voudrais ouvrir un compte bancaire.
back: I'd like to open a bank account.
context: 'Un compte courant' = checking account; 'un compte épargne' = savings account.

front: Quels documents faut-il fournir ?
back: What documents do I need to provide?
context: Usually ID, proof of address ('justificatif de domicile') and sometimes proof of income.

front: Voici mon justificatif de domicile.
back: Here's my proof of address.
context: A recent utility bill or rent receipt.

front: Il me faut un RIB pour mon employeur.
pronunciation: [eel muh foh tan REEB poor mohn nahn-plwah-YUHR]
back: I need my bank details for my employer.
context: 'Un RIB' (relevé d'identité bancaire) = bank details slip with your IBAN. Asked for everything in France.

front: Je voudrais faire un virement.
back: I'd like to make a transfer.

front: J'ai reçu le virement hier.
back: I received the transfer yesterday.

front: Je voudrais retirer de l'argent.
back: I'd like to withdraw some money.

front: Où est le distributeur le plus proche ?
pronunciation: [oo eh luh dees-tree-bü-TUHR luh plü PROSH]
back: Where's the nearest ATM?

front: Le distributeur a avalé ma carte !
back: The ATM swallowed my card!

front: J'ai perdu ma carte bancaire, il faut que je fasse opposition.
pronunciation: [zhay pehr-dü mah kart bahn-KEHR, eel foh kuh zhuh fas oh-poh-zee-SYOHN]
back: I lost my bank card, I need to have it blocked.
context: 'Faire opposition' = to block/cancel a card. 'Il faut que' + subjunctive (fasse). Call your bank right away.

front: Quel est le plafond de retrait ?
back: What's the withdrawal limit?

front: Vous pouvez payer sans contact.
back: You can pay contactless.

front: Tapez votre code, s'il vous plaît.
back: Enter your PIN, please.

front: Mon compte est à découvert.
back: My account is overdrawn.

front: Il y a des frais pour les paiements à l'étranger ?
pronunciation: [eel yah day FREH poor lay peh-mahn ah lay-trahn-ZHAY]
back: Are there fees for payments abroad?

front: Je voudrais changer des dollars en euros.
pronunciation: [zhuh voo-dreh shahn-zhay day doh-LAR ahn nuh-ROH]
back: I'd like to change dollars into euros.

front: Quel est le taux de change aujourd'hui ?
pronunciation: [kel eh luh toh duh SHAHNZH oh-zhoor-DWEE]
back: What's the exchange rate today?
context: 'Le taux' = rate. 'Le taux d'intérêt' = interest rate.

front: Je fais des économies pour acheter une voiture.
pronunciation: [zhuh feh day zay-koh-noh-MEE poor ahsh-tay ün vwah-TÜR]
back: I'm saving up to buy a car.

front: J'ai fait un emprunt pour acheter mon appartement.
pronunciation: [zhay feh tan nahn-PRAN poor ahsh-tay mohn nah-par-tuh-MAHN]
back: I took out a loan to buy my apartment.
context: 'Un emprunt' = loan (from the borrower's side). 'Un prêt immobilier' = mortgage.

front: Les mensualités sont de neuf cents euros.
pronunciation: [lay mahn-sü-ah-lee-TAY sohn duh nuhf sahn zuh-ROH]
back: The monthly payments are nine hundred euros.

front: Je dois prendre rendez-vous avec mon conseiller bancaire.
pronunciation: [zhuh dwah prahn-druh rahn-day-VOO ah-vek mohn kohn-seh-yay bahn-KEHR]
back: I need to make an appointment with my bank adviser.
context: In France each customer usually has a named 'conseiller'.

front: Je consulte mon solde sur l'application.
back: I check my balance on the app.

front: Ce mois-ci, j'ai beaucoup dépensé.
back: This month I spent a lot.

front: Le paiement a été refusé.
back: The payment was declined.

front: Vous pouvez me faire un reçu ?
back: Can you give me a receipt?
context: 'Un reçu' = receipt. For a business: 'une facture' (invoice).

front: Je paie en trois fois sans frais.
pronunciation: [zhuh peh ahn trwah FWAH sahn FREH]
back: I'm paying in three installments, interest-free.
context: 'En trois fois' = in three installments: common in French shops.

front: Le chèque est encore utilisé en France, mais de moins en moins.
pronunciation: [luh SHEK eh tahn-kor ü-tee-lee-ZAY ahn FRAHNS, meh duh mwan zahn MWAN]
back: Checks are still used in France, but less and less.
context: 'De moins en moins' = less and less; 'de plus en plus' = more and more.

front: Je rembourse mon ami demain.
back: I'm paying my friend back tomorrow.

front: Tu peux me prêter vingt euros ?
back: Can you lend me twenty euros?

front: Je t'envoie l'argent par Lydia.
back: I'll send you the money via Lydia.
context: Lydia and Wero are popular French apps for paying friends back.

front: Les impôts sont prélevés à la source.
pronunciation: [lay zan-POH sohn pray-luh-vay ah lah SOORS]
back: Taxes are deducted at source.
context: 'Prélever' = to deduct. Income tax is withheld from salaries in France.

front: J'ai un prélèvement automatique pour le loyer.
pronunciation: [zhay an pray-lev-mahn oh-toh-mah-TEEK poor luh lwah-YAY]
back: I have a direct debit for the rent.

front: Mon salaire tombe le vingt-huit du mois.
pronunciation: [mohn sah-lehr tohmb luh vant-weet dü MWAH]
back: My salary comes in on the 28th of the month.

front: C'est hors de prix !
back: It's outrageously expensive!

front: Ça coûte les yeux de la tête.
pronunciation: [sah koot lay zyuh duh lah TET]
back: It costs an arm and a leg.
context: Literally 'it costs the eyes of the head'.
